subject: Regional activation readiness: roles, sequencing and evidence
messages:
From: Sara Gill <sara.gill@arboretumcap.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: paul.rosenberg@arboretumcap.com
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Arboretum: regional activation sequencing — initial questions

Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround on the questionnaire. A few clarifications so our ops team can map responsibilities:  

1) You indicate a 15-minute RTO for the hosted API control plane in the US-primary region. Is that an upper bound for control-plane failover only or does it include application warm-up for customer-dedicated endpoints?

2) In the "cross-region KV sync" note you reference asynchronous replication and a maximum data-loss window. Can you state the expected RPO in minutes for embeddings and for ephemeral inference state?

3) We'll need an annotated runbook excerpt showing the cutover lead, fallback decision authority, and required preconditions for automated cutover (e.g., healthcheck thresholds). Can you attach something we can present to our SRE team?

Thanks — Sara

--
Sara Gill
VP, IT Ops — Arboretum Capital

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Sara Gill <sara.gill@arboretumcap.com>, paul.rosenberg@arboretumcap.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Arboretum: regional activation sequencing — initial questions

Sara — thanks, good questions. Short answers up front, then I attach detail:  

• Control plane RTO: 15 minutes is the target for control-plane failover (API traffic routing and fleet control). For Dedicated customer endpoints there is an additional warm-up window we account for — typically 5–20 minutes depending on model cold-start (we've captured this as an "endpoint warm-up" step in the matrix).

• RPO: for persistent artifacts (user embeddings, metadata) the expected RPO is <= 2 minutes with cross-region async rep; for ephemeral inference state (KV cache) we treat it as best-effort and assume loss may occur — we provide automatic retry and transparent fallbacks.

• Runbook excerpt attached (runbook-snippets-annotated.pdf) and an activation matrix workbook (redwood-regional-activation-matrix-v1.xlsx) that maps roles. Please see the "Cutover decision" section on tab 2 for authority and thresholds.

I'll also copy our SRE lead, Laura, to scope a brief walkthrough with your team. If you'd like we can schedule a 45-minute run-through this week.

—Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Sara Gill <sara.gill@arboretumcap.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Arboretum: regional activation sequencing — initial questions

Sara / Marcus — adding a couple of operational notes for Arboretum's SREs:  

- Pre-cutover checks: (1) control-plane health > 95% for 10m, (2) KV sync lag < 120s for persistent stores, (3) no active migrations in progress. These are in the workbook as automated gating checks.

- Warm-up strategy: for large models we recommend a staged warm-up (canary endpoints at 2x baseline RPS for 5m, then scale to target). Warm-up is optional for best-effort Dedicated failover but required for SLA-backed Dedicated pools.

- Fallback policy: we maintain a soft-fallback to a multi-region smaller model variant in-hosted tier if dedicated capacity remains unavailable after 30 minutes. This is explained in the runbook appendix.

I'll be available for the walkthrough; propose Wednesday 11:00 PT — Marcus / Sara, does that work?

Laura
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Paul Rosenberg <paul.rosenberg@arboretumcap.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Gill <sara.gill@arboretumcap.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 07:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Arboretum: regional activation sequencing — initial questions

Laura / Marcus — thanks for the materials. A couple follow-ups after a quick internal review:  

1) Can you confirm the expected latency impact to 95th percentile p50 for customer inference when cutover completes? We need conservative numbers for our incident runbooks (ballpark in ms at typical query sizes).

2) For the fallback model variant, do you offer a pre-tested quantized profile (we prefer quantized-INT8) and can you commit to a regression test before enabling fallback routes?

3) We'll need a signed operational SLA appendix that captures enforcement windows for Dedicated vs Hosted tiers; is DocuSign the right way to get that executed?

Paul

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Paul Rosenberg <paul.rosenberg@arboretumcap.com>, Sara Gill <sara.gill@arboretumcap.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Arboretum: regional activation sequencing — initial questions

Paul — quick answers inline:  

1) Latency impact: typical 95th percentile delta for non-quantized medium-size models (2–4k tokens) during steady-state after cutover is +40–120ms. For small models it's consistently <30ms. We include measured deltas per model in the activation matrix (tab 3) so you can pick conservative numbers for your runbooks.

2) Fallback model profiles: yes — we maintain pre-built quantized INT8 profiles for common variants and run a smoke/regression suite prior to enabling any automated fallback. We can commit to a single regression run and provide the report as part of the activation package.

3) SLA appendix via DocuSign is perfect. I'll attach a redline-ready appendix and initiate DocuSign; we can iterate if you have procurement redlines.

I've attached a short checklist (in the workbook) that maps the acceptance gates to sign-off roles.

—Vivek

From: Sara Gill <sara.gill@arboretumcap.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Arboretum: regional activation sequencing — initial questions

Thanks — that covers everything for the first pass. We'll review the workbook and runbook appendix with our SRE on Friday and return any redlines for the DocuSign appendix. I appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample regression commitment; please flag the DocuSign envelope when live.

Best,
Sara
